newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Feb 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Feb 21.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Friday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:

* Johnson Controls reached a tentative three-year contract with the United Auto Workers union to end a 24-day strike at two plants supplying seats for the Expedition, one of Ford's most profitable vehicles.
* ITT Corp is bidding for SEAT SpA, an Italian directory publisher valued at $1.6 billion.
* PepsiCo is in talks to let some of its U.S. bottlers take operating control of some international franchise territories.
* A major shipping cartel said it will raise rates on Asian imports to the United States, following a price war that has caused freight lines to fall more than 10 percent in a year.
* The Dow industrials fell 92.75 to 6,927.38, and Nasdaq slipped 18.18 to 1,347.40. Bonds and the dollar also dropped.
* American Airlines said it will delay delivery of some Boeing jets because a labor settlement with its pilots is at least two months away.

* Prudential Insurance Co of America tentatively agreed to sweeten its proposed settlement of deceptive sales practice allegations to win support for its plan from regulators in Florida, Massachusettes and Texas.
* The Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating claims that Centennial Technologies' former chief executive was fired once before for allegedly inflating a company's results.
* Northeast Utilities said its chairman and chief executive, Bernard Fox, would retire early.
* A former Philip Morris chemist said he was ordered in the 1980s to shred research reports showing higher-than-expected levels of a suspected carcinogen in the company's Virginia Slims cigarettes.
* Coffee futures continued to rise, contributing to a 57 percent increase since the beginning of the year.
* H.F. Ahmanson is moving to ease the furor caused by its plans to lay off Great Western employees if its hostile bid for Great Western is successful.
* CompuServe posted a smaller-than-expected fiscal third quarter loss but said its on-line service continued to lose members.
* General Electric's NBC and Westinghouse's CBS are refusing to run an advertisement for General Motor's Cadillac that includes a star on "NYPD Blue," a show on Walt Disney's ABC.
* For years, investors looked to store shelves full of Rubbermaid's garbage bins and laundry baskets as vital signs of a healthy consumer products giant.

These days, they are beginning to look at something else: resins. More specifically, the price of polypropylene resins, where a penny-a-pound increase translates into a $10 million pretax hit at this Wooster, Ohio, marketer of items from spatulas to Servin Saver food containers. -- Heard on the Street.
* Bonds fell for the third day as traders continued to use the market's recent gains as an opportunity to secure profits. -- Credit Markets.
